item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sun Sep 6 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.description:
Enjoy a 5-star Lancaster County ice cream tour experience with Strasburg Scooter Tours. You’ll see rolling farmlands, pass by horse and buggies, and enjoy some of the best Ice Cream in Lancaster County! It’s a stark contrast to the usual fast-paced and congested areas of larger cities. item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Sep 8, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Amish Fall Farmhouse Experience at Old Windmill Farm — Thu Sep 10 — Old Windmill Farm
item.description:
An autumn afternoon in our farm kitchen. Join us as we bake bread, churn butter from our own cows’ cream, and press apple cider with a traditional hand-cranked apple press. Then sit down and enjoy all three together, with the freshly churned butter on the bread warm from the oven.
Press fresh cider with a traditional press Churn butter from our own cows’ cream Enjoy freshly baked bread Drink cider and eat bread with fresh butter A working farm kitchen, not a demonstration Advance reservations required
Part of the visit is outdoors – dress for the weather. Book This Tour
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Radio Soul! at American Music Theatre — Thu Sep 10, 7:30 PM — American Music Theatre
item.description: Radio Soul! The Early Songs of Elvis Costello – Elvis Costello & The Imposters with Charlie Sexton For over four decades, Elvis Costello has remained one of music’s most fearless and influential songwriters — blending rock, punk, new wave, soul, and pop into a catalog of songs that continue to inspire generations. Now, Costello returns to the stage with The Imposters and special guest Charlie Sexton for Radio Soul!: The Early Songs of Elvis Costello. This unforgettable live performance celebrates the groundbreaking early years of Costello’s career, featuring songs drawn from his first eleven albums — from My Aim Is True through Blood & Chocolate — including fan favorites, deep cuts, and the sharp lyrical storytelling that helped define an era. item.title: Women's Gathering — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Saint James offers opportunities for spiritual growth in smaller group settings that meet every week throughout the year. Whether it is a book group, a Bible study, or a discussion group, we seek to offer diverse offerings to grow deeper in our faith through community and encouragement from each other.
Women’s Gathering is a lay-led group that explores topics related to faith and spiritual practices and periodically seeks outside sources and opportunities to deepen their experience. The Women’s Gathering typically meets on Saturday mornings for fellowship, study, prayer, and worship. Please check the Events Calendar for specific Saturdays each month. The group often meets more often during Advent and Lent. For more information about Women’s Gathering, please email Lorraine Rollo.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: All We Have Is Her Gown: A Historic Pattern Drafter's Discoveries — Sun Sep 20, 2:00 PM — Historic Rock Ford
item.description: Historic Rock Ford’s Fashion of the 18th and 19th Century Lecture Series welcomes Mackenzie Sholtz as she presents “All We Have Is Her Gown: A Historic Pattern Drafter’s Discoveries.” Mackenzie Sholtz received a BA in Medieval Studies from Vassar College and a Certificate of Fashion Design from the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising in San Francisco. She worked in the San Francisco garment industry as a cutter, grader, and pattern drafter for a variety of smaller design houses. A move to South Carolina allowed her to volunteer in Sumter’s local museum which was expanding their educational program to include historic dress. This was the start to her creating her own pattern company focusing on 18th and 19th century women’s clothing based on extant garments in museum and private collections. item.title: Evening Compline — Fri Sep 11, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Oktoberfest Study Hall — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — The Conway Room
item.description:
Raise a stein—and maybe a cocktail, too. Join The Conway Room for an Oktoberfest-inspired Study Hall celebrating the many ways German drinking culture comes to life. We’ll explore Oktoberfest-style beers from around the world while also venturing beyond the beer hall with German-inspired mulled wine and cocktails.
Throughout the evening, you’ll taste, learn, and get hands-on with the drinks, exploring the history, traditions, and flavors behind the celebration. And, as always with Study Hall, you’ll have the opportunity to build a cocktail yourself. Come hungry, because the food is part of the fun. Enjoy hearty housemade fare including mini pretzel sliders featuring cured pork belly, smoked apple jam and sauerkraut, plus housemade bratwurst with beer cheese espuma and curry mustard. Festive activities will round out the evening, making this the perfect excuse to gather your friends, raise a glass, and embrace a little German gemütlichkeit🍺

item.title: Let’s Get Mossy! Fall Kokedama Workshop — Thu Sep 17, 5:30 PM — Gallery Grow
item.description:
Let’s Get Mossy! Create your own fall-inspired Kokedama and learn the art, history, and care behind these living moss ball sculptures. Unwind at the end of your day and join Gallery Grow for an intimate happy hour workshop with expert instruction. As always, BYOB. Slow down, connect with nature, and create your own living work of art.
Kokedama, meaning “moss ball,” is a Japanese botanical art form that transforms a simple plant into a sculptural piece wrapped in living moss. During this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn the history behind Kokedama, create your own moss-covered plant design, and discover how to care for your new living companion. No experience necessary — just bring your creativity and a love for plants!

item.title: What Changed Your Mind? — Sat Sep 26, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society What belief, assumption, or opinion have you genuinely changed your mind about—and what changed it?
Maybe it was religion, politics, science, morality, relationships, gender, economics, or something completely unexpected. Each person will have a few minutes to tell the story of **one thing they once believed and no longer do**, and what evidence, experience, argument, or person caused the shift.
We’ll hear everyone first, without debate or interruption, then open the conversation.
This is not about proving who is right. It’s about something central to freethought: **being willing to reconsider what we think we know.**
Food and drinks available for individual purchase. Here's the menu: https://551west.com/menu/food/
**Attendance is limited to 8, including the organizer.**
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Freethought Society
